# App function reference

Every function your app can call, on one page. Guide links lead to explanations; a dash means there is no guide yet.

Start with the [first-app guide](../getting-started/first-app.md).

## Reading the signatures

A signature gives the return type, function name, and each parameter type and name. `void` means no value is returned. A default such as `durationMs = 0` can be left out of a call. The smaller Example line shows concrete values; copy that call rather than the signature.

| Type or symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `uint8_t` | Whole number from 0 to 255. |
| `int16_t` | Whole number from -32,768 to 32,767. |
| `uint16_t` | Whole number from 0 to 65,535. |
| `int32_t`, `int`, `long` | Signed whole number; on the device, -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647. |
| `uint32_t`, `unsigned long` | Whole number from 0 to 4,294,967,295 on the device; used for elapsed time. |
| `float` | Number that can include a fractional part, such as `0.5f`; about seven significant digits. |
| `bool` | Either `true` or `false`. |
| `const char*`, `String` | Text: a pointer to characters ending with a zero character, or a text object. |
| `const` | The value cannot be changed through this declaration. After a method signature, the method does not change its object. |
| `&` | In a parameter type, a reference to an existing object, rather than a copy; before a value, its address. |
| `*`, `nullptr` | A pointer holds an address; `*` in a declaration marks a pointer, and before a pointer reads the object it points to. `nullptr` means no object. |
| `T` | A type chosen from your arguments; use matching types, such as three `long` values for `constrain()`. |

<style>.function-reference table { table-layout: fixed; width: 100%; } .function-reference th, .function-reference td { min-width: 0 !important; padding: .6em .5em !important; overflow-wrap: anywhere; } .function-reference th:first-child { width: 44%; } .reference-calls th:nth-child(2), .reference-constants th:last-child { width: 42%; } .reference-calls th:last-child, .reference-constants th:nth-child(2) { width: 14%; } .function-reference code { white-space: normal; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }</style>

<div class="function-reference" markdown="1">

These calls are available on both the device and the app emulator. The screen is 128 x 64 pixels with (0, 0) at the top-left; x goes right and y goes down. LEDs are RGBW (red, green, blue, white), with each channel from 0-255.

The calls are written the way they look inside `begin()`, `update()` and `end()` of the studio starter, where `display` (the screen) and `buttonManager` (the buttons) are ready to use. In your own functions at the top of the file, write `HAL::displayProxy()` and `HAL::buttonManager()` instead.

Examples use your own `void onRight(const ButtonEvent& event)` callback (a function called when a button changes), `sprite` image, `sheet`, `animation`, and `player` objects. A button event has `buttonIndex`, `eventType`, and `duration` in ms. Register callbacks in `begin()` and unregister them in `end()`.

!!! tip "Quick answers"
    - [Middle LED blue](#symbol-hal--setrgbled): `HAL::setRgbLed(pixel_Front_Middle, 0, 0, 255, 0);`
    - [Beep](#symbol-audiomanager--playtone): `HAL::audioManager().playTone(880, 100);`
    - [React to the right button](#symbol-buttonmanager--registercallback): `buttonManager.registerCallback(button_RightIndex, onRight);`
    - [Draw text](#symbol-displayproxy--drawstring): `display.drawString(0, 0, "Hi");`
    - [Draw a sprite](#symbol-cf--gfx--drawsprite): `drawSprite(display, sprite, 0, 0);` (after `using namespace cf::gfx;`)
    - [Read the slider](#symbol-sliderposition-percentage-filtered): `sliderPosition_Percentage_Filtered`

| <span id="symbol-degrees"></span>`float degrees(float rad)`<br><small>*Example:* `float angle = degrees(1.0f);`</small> | Convert radians to degrees (360 degrees is one full turn). | [Guide](../concepts/update-loop.md#millis-based-timing-vs-delay) |
| <span id="symbol-millis-now"></span>`unsigned long millis_NOW`<br><small>*Example:* `millis_NOW`</small> | The time in ms when this frame started; read it instead of calling millis() repeatedly. | [Guide](../concepts/update-loop.md#millis-based-timing-vs-delay) |

## Sprites and animation

Studio apps already have `cf_gfx.h` and their generated project art available. You do not need to add those #include lines. Add `using namespace cf::gfx;` at the top of the file, below the #include lines, to use these short names.

When building an app into the firmware by hand, add `#include "cf_gfx.h"` and your generated asset header (if your project has art) at the top of the file. Then put `using namespace cf::gfx;` below the #include lines.

Examples use `Actor player`, `AnimationPlayer clock`, `MeshActor model`, and `RigActor figure`. A pivot is the point on a sprite placed at its screen position.
